scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Derived from concepts of divine childhood, Nepal's Baalan dance translates epics like the Ramayana into spontaneous village performances anchored by the khaijadi drum.
on_screen: Title card: Baalan Dance · Nepal · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The term 'Balan' stems from the Sanskrit word 'Balak' and Nepali 'Bala' meaning child, combined with 'Aayan' to suggest 'Balayan'—narratives of divine childhood.

The tradition developed within Nepal's Brahmin and Chhetri communities as a dramatic medium to enact stories from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, serving as a source of joy and spiritual reflection.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Baalan is performed during holy days such as Ekadashi, Chandi Purnima, and Balachaturdashi, as well as ceremonies like Satyanarayan Puja and Bhagwat Puran.
It acts as both an act of religious worship and a spontaneous social activity enjoyed during periods of rest from work.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danced in group formations, participants move in rhythmic alignment while singing devotional songs.
Dancers enact dramatic roles from religious epics, using representative props and expressive gestures.
A beginner begins by matching simple step patterns to the pulse of the khaijadi drum while joining the vocal chorus.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The musical core consists of devotional bhajans praising deities like Ram, Krishna, and Vishnu.
Rhythmic structure is provided primarily by the khaijadi, a traditional drum, which guides both the tempo and the vocal cadence of the group.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performances occur in sacred settings like temple grounds and domestic courtyards during pujas, as well as open rural spaces.
Dancers wear traditional regional dress and use specific implements corresponding to the epic characters they portray.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Maintained primarily by Brahmin and Chhetri communities in Nepal, who pass down the vocal repertoire, drumming patterns, and theatrical roles through religious gatherings and community participation.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Performed as a religious offering during pujas and sacred festivals. Outsiders should observe respectfully during ritual ceremonies such as Satyanarayan Puja and avoid interrupting the devotional singing or sacred proceedings.
